definitions.HOUSE: A structure built or serving as an abode of human beings.
definitions.WALL: A rampart of earth, stones etc. built up for defensive purposes.
definitions.DOOR: A portal of entry into a building, room, or vehicle, consisting of a rigid plane movable on a hinge.
definitions.ROOF: The external covering at the top of a building.
definitions.FLOOR: The interior bottom or surface of a house or building; the supporting surface of a room.
definitions.STAIR: A single step in a staircase.
definitions.BATH: A tub or pool which is used for bathing: bathtub.
definitions.BED: A piece of furniture, usually flat and soft, on which to rest or sleep.
definitions.DESK: A table, frame, or case, in past centuries usually with a sloping top but now usually with a flat top, for the use of writers and readers.
definitions.CHAIR: An item of furniture used to sit on or in, comprising a seat, legs, back, and sometimes arm rests, for use by one person.
definitions.TABLE: Furniture with a top surface to accommodate a variety of uses.
definitions.COUCH: Couch grass, a species of persistent grass, Elymus repens, usually considered a weed.
definitions.LAMP: A device that generates heat, light or other radiation.
definitions.RUG: A partial covering for a floor.
definitions.MAT: A flat piece of coarse material used for wiping one’s feet, or as a decorative or protective floor covering.
definitions.BOX: Senses relating to a three-dimensional object or space.
definitions.BIN: A box, frame, crib, or enclosed place, used as a storage container.
definitions.CUP: A concave vessel for drinking from, usually made of opaque material (as opposed to a glass) and with a handle.
definitions.DISH: A vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food, often flat with a depressed region in the middle.
definitions.BOWL: A roughly hemispherical container used to hold, mix or present food, such as salad, fruit or soup, or other items.
definitions.FORK: A pronged tool having a long straight handle, used for digging, lifting, throwing etc.
definitions.KNIFE: A utensil or a tool designed for cutting, consisting of a flat piece of hard material, usually steel or other metal (the blade), usually sharpened on one edge, attached to a handle.
definitions.SPOON: An implement for eating or serving; a scooped utensil whose long handle is straight, in contrast to a ladle.
definitions.POT: A flat-bottomed vessel (usually metal) used for cooking food.
definitions.PAN: A wide, flat receptacle used around the house, especially for cooking.
definitions.OVEN: A chamber used for baking or heating.
definitions.SINK: A basin used for holding water for washing.
definitions.TUB: A flat-bottomed vessel, of width similar to or greater than its height, used for storing or packing things, or for washing things in.
definitions.SHOWER: A brief fall of precipitation (spell of rain, or a similar fall of snow, sleet, or cascade).
definitions.SOAP: A substance able to mix with both oil and water, used for cleaning, often in the form of a solid bar or in liquid form, derived from fats or made synthetically.
definitions.TOWEL: A cloth used for wiping, especially one used for drying anything wet, as a person after a bath.
definitions.COMB: A toothed implement for grooming the hair or (formerly) for keeping it in place.
definitions.BRUSH: An implement consisting of multiple more or less flexible bristles or other filaments attached to a handle, used for any of various purposes including cleaning, painting, and arranging hair.
definitions.MIRROR: A smooth surface, usually made of glass with reflective material painted on the underside, that reflects light so as to give an image of what is in front of it.
definitions.CLOCK: An instrument used to measure or keep track of time.
definitions.KEY: An object designed to open and close a lock.
definitions.LOCK: Something used for fastening, which can only be opened with a key or combination.
definitions.BOOK: A collection of sheets of paper bound together to hinge at one edge, containing printed or written material, pictures, etc.
definitions.PEN: An enclosure (enclosed area) used to contain domesticated animals, especially sheep or cattle.
definitions.PAPER: A sheet material used for writing on or printing on (or as a non-waterproof container), usually made by draining cellulose fibres from a suspension in water.
definitions.PHONE: A device for transmitting conversations and other sounds in real time across distances, now often a small portable unit also capable of running software etc.
definitions.TOY: Something to play with, especially as intended for use by a child.
definitions.CLOTH: A woven fabric such as used in dressing, decorating, cleaning or other practical use.
definitions.SHOE: A protective covering for the foot, with a bottom part composed of thick leather or plastic sole and often a thicker heel, and a softer upper part made of leather or synthetic material.
definitions.SOCK: A knitted or woven covering for the foot.
definitions.HAT: A covering for the head, often in the approximate form of a cone or a cylinder closed at its top end, and sometimes having a brim and other decoration.
definitions.BAG: A flexible container made of cloth, paper, plastic, etc.
definitions.KITCHEN: A room or area for preparing food.
definitions.PANTRY: A small room, closet, or cabinet usually located in or near the kitchen, dedicated to shelf-stable food storage and/or storing kitchenware, like a larder, but smaller.
definitions.FREEZER: An appliance or room used to store food or other perishable items at temperatures below 0° Celsius (32° Fahrenheit).
definitions.TOASTER: One who toasts (cooks lightly by browning).
definitions.BLENDER: A machine outfitted with sharp blades, for mashing, crushing or liquefying food ingredients.
definitions.MIXER: One who, or a device that, mixes or merges things together.
definitions.KETTLE: A vessel for boiling a liquid or cooking food, usually metal and equipped with a lid.
definitions.COFFEE: A beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water.
definitions.TEA: A drug smoked or ingested for euphoric effect, cannabis.
definitions.BEDROOM: A room in a house where a bed is kept for sleeping.
definitions.PILLOW: A soft cushion used to support the head in bed.
definitions.BLANKET: A heavy, loosely woven fabric, usually large and woollen, used for warmth while sleeping or resting.
definitions.SHEET: A thin bed cloth used as a covering for a mattress or as a layer over the sleeper.
definitions.CLOSET: Any private area, (particularly) bowers in the open air.
definitions.DRAWER: An open-topped box that can be slid in and out of the cabinet that contains it, used for storing clothing or other articles.
definitions.HANGER: One who hangs, or causes to be hanged; a hangman, paper hanger, etc.
definitions.CABINET: A storage closet either separate from, or built into, a wall.
definitions.SHELF: A flat, rigid structure, fixed at right angles to a wall or forming a part of a cabinet, desk etc., and used to support, store or display objects.
definitions.FRAME: The structural elements of a building or other constructed object.
definitions.WASHER: Something that washes; especially an appliance such as a washing machine or dishwasher.
definitions.DRYER: One who, or that which, dries; a desiccative.
definitions.IRON: A common, inexpensive metal, silvery grey when untarnished, that rusts, is attracted by magnets, and is used in making steel.
definitions.BASKET: A lightweight container, generally round, open at the top, and tapering toward the bottom.
definitions.BROOM: A domestic utensil with fibers bound together at the end of a long handle, used for sweeping.
definitions.VACUUM: A region of space that contains no matter.
definitions.MOP: An implement for washing floors, or the like, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle.
definitions.TRASH: Useless things to be discarded; rubbish; refuse.
definitions.WINDOW: The inedible parts of a grain-producing plant.
definitions.BLIND: A covering for a window to keep out light.
definitions.CURTAIN: A piece of cloth covering a window, bed, etc. to offer privacy and keep out light.
definitions.SHUTTER: One who shuts or closes something.
definitions.PORCH: A covered and enclosed entrance to a building, whether taken from the interior, and forming a sort of vestibule within the main wall, or projecting without and with a separate roof.
definitions.PATIO: A paved outside area, adjoining a house, used for dining or recreation.
definitions.GARAGE: A building (or section of a building) used to store a car or cars, tools and other miscellaneous items.
definitions.ATTIC: The space, often unfinished and with sloped walls, directly below the roof in the uppermost part of a house or other building, generally used for storage or habitation.
definitions.CELLAR: An enclosed underground space, often under a building, used for storage or shelter.
definitions.BASEMENT: A floor of a building below ground level.
definitions.GARDEN: An outdoor area containing one or more types of plants, usually plants grown for food or ornamental purposes.
definitions.FENCE: A thin artificial barrier that separates two pieces of land or a house perimeter.
definitions.GATE: A doorlike structure outside a house.
definitions.YARD: A small, usually uncultivated area adjoining or (now especially) within the precincts of a house or other building.
definitions.DRIVE: Motivation to do or achieve something; ability coupled with ambition.
definitions.CHIMNEY: A vertical tube or hollow column used to emit environmentally polluting gaseous and solid matter (including but not limited to by-products of burning carbon or hydrocarbon based fuels); a flue.
definitions.HEATER: A device that produces and radiates heat, typically to raise the temperature of a room or building.
definitions.COOLER: Having a slightly low temperature; mildly or pleasantly cold.
definitions.REMOTE: An element of broadcast programming originating away from the station's or show's control room.
